![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/1b3a9a3891150ae0b187c79e2305d391f719898a9efe42b42e7bf0777d965aa3.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1)$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>-a)=P(Z<a)=Φ(a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z<2.22).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/2efe9f4a4ac7f5bc307ef3e13d5f53f39be0143de2f33d87887235bc37410c94.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z>-2.22).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/94537e936e6fcb151fb8d61a3cd118bc8b1caaa609777c2eb0d363fc1063c885.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z<2.22) & =P(Z>-2.22) \\  & =1-P(Z<-2.22) \\  & =1-Φ(-2.22) \\  & =1-0.0132 \\  & =0.9868.\end{aligned}
$$
